title: persona-config
description: Copied to .claude/persona-config.json by install-antislop. The hook scripts read this at runtime via ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}-relative scripts + a project-relative config path, so the plugin's hook scripts stay generic across every project.

testAndLintCommand.description: Single test+lint shell command (no longer run by stop-gate). e.g. 'npm test && npm run lint'

lintCommand.description: Formatter/linter invoked on a single changed file, e.g. 'npx eslint --fix'. The file path is appended as the last argument.

graphUpdateCommand.description: Code Review Graph's incremental-update command, taking a file path argument, e.g. 'code-review-graph update' (a pip/pipx-installed CLI, not npx - verify the current command at ADAPT time)

sourceGlobs.description: Shell glob patterns, PROJECT-ROOT-RELATIVE (not absolute), identifying source files worth graph-indexing. The hook normalizes the tool's absolute file_path against CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR before matching. If empty, every edited file is passed to graphUpdateCommand.

protectedPaths.description: Shell glob patterns, PROJECT-ROOT-RELATIVE (not absolute - e.g. 'supabase/migrations/*', not '/home/u/proj/supabase/migrations/*'), for paths requiring explicit human approval before Write/Edit. Entries may be a bare glob string (legacy shape, still supported by the reader), or an object with 'pattern' (required) plus optional 'tag'/'reason' for the server-mirror-eligible/local-only E8 tagging contract. Examples: 'supabase/migrations/*', {"pattern": "*.lock", "tag": "local-only", "reason": "..."}

gatedAgents.description: Agent-type names whose SubagentStop raises a pending-review flag (and whose dispatch touches the writer-dispatch stamp for stop-gate.sh's marker check). Defaults to just lead-programmer. Add a persona name here if you add a new code-writing persona - this is a config edit, not a plugin file edit. Matching is namespace-insensitive: both this config's entries and the incoming agent-identity payload are canonicalized to their bare persona name before comparing, so an entry written as 'lead-programmer' also matches a namespaced payload like 'antislop:lead-programmer', and an entry written as 'antislop:lead-programmer' also matches a bare 'lead-programmer' payload. You never need to list both forms.

humanReviewMode.description: Retired in 0.32.0 and ignored; the reviewer may add a needs-human note instead.

defaultImplementerModel.description: The lead-programmer model tier the orchestrator dispatches on when a unit carries no per-dispatch `Suggested model` tag. Precedence is per-dispatch tag > this config field > agents/lead-programmer.md's frontmatter default. Already-adapted projects have this field backfilled by `runUpdate` when absent, using the packaged agents/lead-programmer.md frontmatter default (unit item18-2). An ABSENT key resolves to the packaged frontmatter default - only after backfill skips or for projects predating the backfill. An unrecognised value also resolves toward MORE capability, never less (i.e. "opus") - same fail-toward-more-capability direction as humanReviewMode's own absent/unrecognised-value fallback. A "sonnet" value recorded before the haiku default shipped is migrated once to "haiku" by --update (bin/cli.js migrateDefaultImplementerModel).

knowledgeWrites.description: Whether scribe and spec-master may edit CONTEXT.md, docs/harness-glossary.md, README.md and docs/adr/ outside a unit's scope. "scoped" (the default; also an ABSENT key and any unrecognised value) turns such edits into knowledge proposals in the persona's report; "apply" lets them edit directly. --update never backfills this key; set it with --update --knowledge-writes=<scoped|apply>.

orchestratorModel.description: The model of the main session, which runs as the orchestrator. Rendered into .claude/agents/orchestrator.md's frontmatter `model:` line by install and by `--update --force-render`. Absent: the shipped `model: sonnet`. `inherit` keeps your own session model (the behaviour before qw-u6). An unrecognised value keeps the shipped model and prints a note.

pluginVersion.description: The antislop plugin version this project was last ADAPTed/updated at, stamped by install-antislop. Compared against the installed plugin's current version by the SessionStart drift-check hook.

personaSelection.description: Which optional personas (spec-master, scribe, reviewer, researcher, milestone-auditor, agent-auditor) this project chose to include, recorded by install-antislop' persona-selection wizard so --update mode knows which files to re-derive. orchestrator/explorer/lead-programmer are always included and not listed here.

issueTracker.description: Human-readable note on the tracker chosen during ADAPT, e.g. 'GitHub issues labeled plan/<slug>; fetch with gh issue list --label plan/<slug>' or 'local files in docs/plans/<slug>/issues/'

substitutions.description: Deterministic substitution values recorded at ADAPT time so `bin/cli.js --update` can regenerate a byte-identical fresh copy of each version-stamped file directly from the plugin's own source, with no LLM involved. Absent (or missing sub-fields) on projects adapted before this field existed - `--update` falls back to the LLM-driven `/install-antislop --update` flow for those, which also backfills this field.

graphMcpLaunch.description: The code-review-graph MCP launch command inlined into explorer.md's mcpServers frontmatter at ADAPT time (install-antislop step 4, or `bin/cli.js --wire-graph-mcp`, which extracts this straight from the tool-generated project-wide .mcp.json). `env` is optional and only present if the server's .mcp.json entry had one. Null if the graph was never wired.

arxivMcpLaunch.description: The arXiv MCP launch command inlined into researcher.md's mcpServers frontmatter (install-antislop step 5, or `bin/cli.js --wire-arxiv-mcp <server-key>` once a server is installed). Null if researcher wasn't selected, or was selected but no working MCP was found (WebFetch/WebSearch fallback mode).

fileHashes.description: sha256 hex digest of each version-stamped file's content with its stamp line stripped, recorded immediately after ADAPT/--update finishes writing it. `--update` compares this against the project's current file (stamp stripped) to detect local edits without an LLM: matching hash means safe to silently regenerate at the new version; a mismatch means a human is asked before overwriting. Keyed by project-relative path, e.g. '.claude/agents/spec-master.md'.

dispatchHygiene.description: Configuration for dispatch hygiene gates that prevent problematic Agent spawns. Absent object ⇒ defaults apply (mode: "block"). Set mode to "off" to disable all checks.

maxPromptBytes.description: Maximum dispatch prompt size in bytes. Calibrated to 2× the observed maximum (14898) as of 2026-07-30 from a measured corpus of 26 contract dispatch prompts.

maxInlineBlockLines.description: Maximum interior lines of a fenced code block in a dispatch prompt. Calibrated to 2× the observed maximum (41) as of 2026-07-30 from a measured corpus of 26 contract dispatch prompts.

markerCommitCheck.description: Configuration for the marker-commit-check.sh classifier run by hand (no longer run by stop-gate), which flags a PASS marker's commit: field as possibly citing a commit that does not belong to its unit. Absent object ⇒ mode: "warn" - deliberately differs from dispatchHygiene's "block" default, since ~1-2% of mismatch classifications are hard false positives and a false block on a gate the reviewer does not own is worse than a missed warning.

mode.description: Posture on a mismatch classification: "warn" (one-line stderr warning, exit path unchanged), "block" (exit 2, pending-review flags left standing so the reviewer gets a second attempt), or "off" (skip the classifier call entirely - no audit line at all). "ok"/"unverifiable" states are always silent apart from the audit line, in every mode.

reviewGating.description: Review gating switch (user-facing name: gateless mode). "off" makes reviewer verdicts advisory and the review-enforcement gates inert (stop-gate.sh's pending-review flags and marker check, reviewer-route-gate.sh's unit-exclusivity block and .review-join.* stamps); protection gates stay armed.

mode.description: Resolution rule: only the exact string off disables; absent, unreadable or any other value resolves to enforce.
